newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiris strike on Bangladesh's 25th anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiris strike on Bangladesh's 25th anniversary.

text.p: Shops and businesses were shut in Kashmir's biggest city Srinagar on Monday after separatist guerrillas called a strike to mark the 25th anniversary of Bangladeshi independence.

"We are not against the creation of Bangladesh but we want the people of Kashmir to protest strongly against the Indian conspiracy to divide the Moslems of the sub-continent," the Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen, a Kashmiri separatist group, said.
The Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen is one of dozens of separatist groups fighting for Kashmir's independence or merger with Pakistan.
More than 50,000 people have died since an Islamic separatist revolt broke out in Kashmir in 1990, state Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah has estimated.

On December 16, 1971, India accepted the surrender of about 90,000 Pakistani soldiers in Dhaka after a 14-day-war between the two countries that led to the creation of Bangladesh, most of whose people are Moslem.
A separatist women's group, the Dukhtaran-e-Millat (Daughters of the Nation), hoisted black banners in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
"The fall of Dhaka is such a great tragedy for the Moslem world that mere words fail to express our condolence," Asia Andrabi, the group's leader, said in a statement.
"The Kashmiris are mourning the fall of Dhaka. It's quite amazing. It's the first time I've seen it in my life," said a local journalist.
India and neighbouring Pakistan have fought two of their three wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
